## The invitation lifecycle

**1. Before creation, on the members settings page.** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/members/page.tsx` loads the tenant context and checks `can(actor, "member:invite", …)` before it even renders the invite form. The client component `src/components/domain/member/invite-member-form.tsx` (`InviteMemberForm`) redundantly re-checks `can(...)` for UX (not real enforcement), validates the typed email/role against `inviteMemberSchema` (`src/schemas/member.ts`), and disables submission if the org is out of seats (`seatCheck.exceeded`). Submitting calls the server action `inviteMemberAction` in `src/actions/members/invite-member.ts`, wrapped by `withAction(inviteMemberSchema, handler, ...)`, which re-parses the input with Zod, re-checks the `member:invite` permission (now with a real `PENDING_MEMBER_ID` resource), enforces `consumeRateLimit(orgId, "member:invite")`, and re-derives seat usage via `getOrganizationSummary`/`getPlanLimits` to reject if the invite would exceed the plan's seat limit. It then delegates to the service layer, `inviteMembers` in `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts`, which repeats org-scope assertion, permission check, rate limiting, and a seat check that counts *both* active members (`memberRepo.countActiveMembers`) and pending invitations (`invitationRepo.countPendingInvitations`) — so pending invites consume seats too. There is no explicit "already invited" dedup beyond a non-unique `(orgId, email)` index.

**2. What's stored vs. what travels in the link.** For each invite, `inviteMembers` generates a raw 32-byte token with `randomToken(32)` (`src/lib/hash.ts`, `crypto.randomBytes(...).toString("base64url")`), but only `hashToken(token)` — a SHA-256 hex digest — is persisted via `invitationRepo.insertInvitation`. The `invitations` table (`src/server/db/schema/members.ts`) stores `orgId`, `email`, `role`, `invitedBy`, `tokenHash`, `expiresAt` (14 days out), `acceptedAt`, and `revokedAt`, with a unique index on `tokenHash`. The raw token itself is never written to the database — it exists only in the invite link (`/invite/[token]`), so a DB leak alone can't be used to accept invitations. (Note: in this codebase snapshot, no call site actually renders `InviteEmail`/sends the mail — `inviteMembers` only calls `emit("member.invited", ...)`, which the activity service turns into an audit-log entry; email delivery of the link appears unwired.)

**3. When the link is used.** `src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx` only checks the token's *shape* against `invitationTokenSchema` (`src/schemas/invitation.ts`, `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/`, length 32–128) — deliberately no DB lookup at this stage. It requires a signed-in session (`getSessionPrincipal()`, redirecting to `/login?next=...` otherwise) and renders `InviteAcceptForm`, which calls the server action `acceptInvitationAction` (`src/actions/members/accept-invitation.ts`). That action re-parses the token, confirms the session principal, and calls `acceptInvitation(userId, { token })` in the service layer. `acceptInvitation` hashes the incoming token and looks it up by `hashToken` via `invitationRepo.findInvitationByTokenHash` — the one repository call deliberately unscoped by `orgId`, since "the hash carries the tenant with it." It then checks `revokedAt`, `acceptedAt` (idempotent re-accept if already a member), and `expiresAt` against the current time before proceeding.

**4. What happens once membership exists.** On success, `memberRepo.insertMember` writes the actual membership row, `invitationRepo.markInvitationAccepted` closes out the invitation, and `emit("member.joined", ...)` fires through the in-process event bus (`src/lib/event-bus.ts`, wired at boot by `registerEventHandlers()` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`). Two listeners react: `usage-service.ts` increments the org's `seatsUsed` counter, and `notification-service.ts` creates an in-app notification for the org owner. There's no `member.joined` activity-log listener, so acceptance itself isn't separately audit-logged (only `member.invited` is). There's also no permission/session cache to invalidate — `resolveActor(userId, orgId)` in `src/server/services/member-service.ts` re-reads membership fresh from the DB on every request, so the new role is visible immediately. Back in `acceptInvitationAction`, `assertSeatAvailable` re-derives the `Actor` post-acceptance and re-validates the org isn't over its seat limit before the client redirects into the workspace.
